### Main Metabolic Steps

- **Step 1 (Ethanol to Acetaldehyde):** Enzymes—primarily **alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH)** —convert ethanol into **acetaldehyde** , a toxic compound and known carcinogen. Higher alcohol levels or chronic drinking also recruit **cytochrome P450 2E1 (CYP2E1)** and catalase.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXfEtLADXY0vs0lPmo-fInIoV4WPAiLzJapt8JIiXjRYOF6GnPYSEuFwrbd_TBhwHNfm0NCzAYQemMVuKL_Ln-JzaT1MHXmWksY4NtLXaENeaF2tyYJ16_tegPRaKyNmnI5nkmf79vrfo1DLVIQuVgFVc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXfwbe6mWrGLbgVKB7YShrAXjYxMWER6_WTZzxQt6R6sHBWLmhHdplX1r-aop4BKaEKFNdt4nWYKyzdN7eeZbEYBDHFc6gCGBYIKE8Et7hdHIUAPow0wVrMsXQkOG6x0_aYb00xtZicnyr)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStgEBxCJF17pRuW_UzZdrZFa7LOhxGts6Wpw0Izk34YWk_AlxXzqxyJgCNQIpVXS-Cv6u_Xbp_MPod9T7G-0GZ55EMjA9b-29dKUB7kspAxYlQiBWLNQN3l4TT-AbDbW3A9_qGOZULUjIGYlhNy6XkSoe-E05npQ40gF4GDdAQ2FWrrEWWO6473EUMyy5zhzf027lSh239y5q8xk8k0FvZIGL896qCED5fctFKOOeI7TVyTWezn0IdQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF1-Kv97J2AnnLUNUWzOjFu4zw-YsuxJi4pVx5aWV_qOLw4caUel2iN9vWz0gqdR0wtbQVy36raTDFXCSRRm0qxhD_J2KjPl_d556HloOmgB-WXPkE56l4U3iwiE-VWNYturuZv1ai0LCdAJ7sHQq8gQ2mCEc1rUctr_43NRMpm3js8r_BO8St)
- **Step 2 (Acetaldehyde to Acetate):** **Aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH)** , mainly mitochondrial ALDH2, rapidly turns acetaldehyde into **acetate**.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF1-Kv97J2AnnLUNUWzOjFu4zw-YsuxJi4pVx5aWV_qOLw4caUel2iN9vWz0gqdR0wtbQVy36raTDFXCSRRm0qxhD_J2KjPl_d556HloOmgB-WXPkE56l4U3iwiE-VWNYturuZv1ai0LCdAJ7sHQq8gQ2mCEc1rUctr_43NRMpm3js8r_BO8St)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXfEtLADXY0vs0lPmo-fInIoV4WPAiLzJapt8JIiXjRYOF6GnPYSEuFwrbd_TBhwHNfm0NCzAYQemMVuKL_Ln-JzaT1MHXmWksY4NtLXaENeaF2tyYJ16_tegPRaKyNmnI5nkmf79vrfo1DLVIQuVgFVc)
- **Final Clearance:** Acetate enters the bloodstream and breaks down into carbon dioxide and water, largely in tissues outside the liver.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStgEBxCJF17pRuW_UzZdrZFa7LOhxGts6Wpw0Izk34YWk_AlxXzqxyJgCNQIpVXS-Cv6u_Xbp_MPod9T7G-0GZ55EMjA9b-29dKUB7kspAxYlQiBWLNQN3l4TT-AbDbW3A9_qGOZULUjIGYlhNy6XkSoe-E05npQ40gF4GDdAQ2FWrrEWWO6473EUMyy5zhzf027lSh239y5q8xk8k0FvZIGL896qCED5fctFKOOeI7TVyTWezn0IdQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXfEtLADXY0vs0lPmo-fInIoV4WPAiLzJapt8JIiXjRYOF6GnPYSEuFwrbd_TBhwHNfm0NCzAYQemMVuKL_Ln-JzaT1MHXmWksY4NtLXaENeaF2tyYJ16_tegPRaKyNmnI5nkmf79vrfo1DLVIQuVgFVc)
- **Minor Pathway:** A small fraction forms non-oxidative metabolites (such as fatty acid ethyl esters and phosphatidylethanol) that linger longer in tissues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXcGNMlT_-BwqYHVoXYgUQvV9EZXtcDq4Kr1jRRRQ_ZVGRRccn8z5D5ltnFOwx9HJiUT6oVt1lzUrbefotVU_Z_eSpi5Zw1IPUlcEljJ1jD3UmM2F7hSTJQ58ioPp-h6QO8Vb-XH8a2CEmLlSILp_vz7PcjhXHTIt4xw)

### Rate and Limits

- **Steady Pace:** The liver processes alcohol at a relatively fixed rate—often roughly one standard drink per hour or about a **0.015% drop in blood alcohol concentration (BAC) per hour** —limited largely by how fast the cell regenerates **NAD+** from NADH.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF18NPG4c9iLESqia62bc6vXDUvn3q6X8ib8TkFs8bkzPIPglePIaCy21aL_xTSVn_fp0ipGmogkc9sxv1SiThImz5DtQ6pIzxMn_ISpdf7p4acMXnQozBaE7EPRKKSQKwFSqp0_wVkrxfg7nvfJfSGihkk3nNLeQfJNOkrPxpprGeXfBr1inQbnTm6tNmBURtg4i6z6mHvOYH)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1-0VySC28zJekLM2nofDfldzN_6uhbx4d7paVrD2dOOupUfBQ-3hBWWD_4mHSV10YkcEWT56fSrByuAohkM-LJqGrT_3vbOPeoRNzsMWZuGNhEyHr2EQG0TqbtgsK2bB4tVfBkTzLlAoQoVGxj0YMH7NRweqKR9l9aqMaLVLZlY)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TCBW-Nidevk&t=40)
- **What Changes It:** Liver disease, certain medications (like acetaminophen), and genetics can slow clearance or shift how byproducts accumulate. Coffee, showers, or sleep do not speed up liver metabolism.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXfEtLADXY0vs0lPmo-fInIoV4WPAiLzJapt8JIiXjRYOF6GnPYSEuFwrbd_TBhwHNfm0NCzAYQemMVuKL_Ln-JzaT1MHXmWksY4NtLXaENeaF2tyYJ16_tegPRaKyNmnI5nkmf79vrfo1DLVIQuVgFVc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStgEBxCJF17pRuW_UzZdrZFa7LOhxGts6Wpw0Izk34YWk_AlxXzqxyJgCNQIpVXS-Cv6u_Xbp_MPod9T7G-0GZ55EMjA9b-29dKUB7kspAxYlQiBWLNQN3l4TT-AbDbW3A9_qGOZULUjIGYlhNy6XkSoe-E05npQ40gF4GDdAQ2FWrrEWWO6473EUMyy5zhzf027lSh239y5q8xk8k0FvZIGL896qCED5fctFKOOeI7TVyTWezn0IdQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF18NPG4c9iLESqia62bc6vXDUvn3q6X8ib8TkFs8bkzPIPglePIaCy21aL_xTSVn_fp0ipGmogkc9sxv1SiThImz5DtQ6pIzxMn_ISpdf7p4acMXnQozBaE7EPRKKSQKwFSqp0_wVkrxfg7nvfJfSGihkk3nNLeQfJNOkrPxpprGeXfBr1inQbnTm6tNmBURtg4i6z6mHvOYH)

### Why It Can Harm the Liver

- **Acetaldehyde Toxicity:** Acetaldehyde can damage DNA and bind to proteins, disrupting liver cell structure and function.
- **Oxidative Stress and Fat Buildup:** Excess NADH, altered fat metabolism, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) from CYP2E1 promote fat accumulation in liver cells (steatosis), inflammation, scarring (fibrosis/cirrhosis), and liver cancer over time.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vo3-xyRgb4E)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXfwbe6mWrGLbgVKB7YShrAXjYxMWER6_WTZzxQt6R6sHBWLmhHdplX1r-aop4BKaEKFNdt4nWYKyzdN7eeZbEYBDHFc6gCGBYIKE8Et7hdHIUAPow0wVrMsXQkOG6x0_aYb00xtZicnyr)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF1-Kv97J2AnnLUNUWzOjFu4zw-YsuxJi4pVx5aWV_qOLw4caUel2iN9vWz0gqdR0wtbQVy36raTDFXCSRRm0qxhD_J2KjPl_d556HloOmgB-WXPkE56l4U3iwiE-VWNYturuZv1ai0LCdAJ7sHQq8gQ2mCEc1rUctr_43NRMpm3js8r_BO8St)

For a plain-language overview of enzymes and byproducts, see the [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXfEtLADXY0vs0lPmo-fInIoV4WPAiLzJapt8JIiXjRYOF6GnPYSEuFwrbd_TBhwHNfm0NCzAYQemMVuKL_Ln-JzaT1MHXmWksY4NtLXaENeaF2tyYJ16_tegPRaKyNmnI5nkmf79vrfo1DLVIQuVgFVc) . items.text: Acetaldehyde Toxicity: Acetaldehyde can damage DNA and bind to proteins, disrupting liver cell structure and function. Oxidative Stress and Fat Buildup: Excess NADH, altered fat metabolism, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) from CYP2E1 promote fat accumulation in liver cells (steatosis), inflammation, scarring (fibrosis/cirrhosis), and liver cancer over time.
items.markdown:
- **Acetaldehyde Toxicity:** Acetaldehyde can damage DNA and bind to proteins, disrupting liver cell structure and function.
- **Oxidative Stress and Fat Buildup:** Excess NADH, altered fat metabolism, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) from CYP2E1 promote fat accumulation in liver cells (steatosis), inflammation, scarring (fibrosis/cirrhosis), and liver cancer over time.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vo3-xyRgb4E)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXfwbe6mWrGLbgVKB7YShrAXjYxMWER6_WTZzxQt6R6sHBWLmhHdplX1r-aop4BKaEKFNdt4nWYKyzdN7eeZbEYBDHFc6gCGBYIKE8Et7hdHIUAPow0wVrMsXQkOG6x0_aYb00xtZicnyr)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF1-Kv97J2AnnLUNUWzOjFu4zw-YsuxJi4pVx5aWV_qOLw4caUel2iN9vWz0gqdR0wtbQVy36raTDFXCSRRm0qxhD_J2KjPl_d556HloOmgB-WXPkE56l4U3iwiE-VWNYturuZv1ai0LCdAJ7sHQq8gQ2mCEc1rUctr_43NRMpm3js8r_BO8St)
